messages:
rachael: Thanks everyone for joining. Quick follow-up from the headcount slide — will transfers be immediate or staged?
sam: staged, right? would like clarity on who owns the "handoff" for ongoing projects.
rachael: staged — we want minimal disruption. high-level plan: 1) identify critical roles, 2) freeze hires for non-critical buckets for 4 weeks, 3) execute transfers in 2 waves.
alex: can you define "critical" and who signs off? product infra/security?
rachael: critical = customer-facing infra, active SLAs, and open enterprise deals where we risk delivery. sign-off is Lina (People Ops) + relevant hiring manager + Matt for cross-org escalations.
lina: confirming — sign-off matrix will be posted to the People Ops repo today. quick snippet of the transfer policy we'll publish: 
```
TRANSFER WINDOW: 2026-04-01 -> 2026-05-15
PRIORITY BUCKETS: infra, security, enterprise success
HIRING FREEZE: non-priority buckets pause for 4 weeks
EXCEPTIONS: by approval only (Lina + hiring manager + exec)
```
sam: thanks. what's the expected notice to impacted folks and does team X keep on-call during transition?
rachael: 2 weeks notice for individuals. operational continuity is required — teams must keep on-call and we expect a 2-week shadow handoff where possible.
hema: recruiter bandwidth question — do we pause new reqs entirely or let recruiting continue to pipeline? we have offers in flight.
lina: recruiting should continue for offers already extended and for priority buckets. non-priority reqs should be deprioritized but not cancelled until offers are final. we'll add a flag in Greenhouse ("transfer-sensitive") this afternoon.
alex: can we get a clear timeline for role-level decisions? some managers need headcount to plan Q3 roadmaps.
matt: rough timeline: decisions for priority roles by 2026-04-08, wave-1 transfers executed by 2026-04-22, wave-2 completed by 2026-05-15. managers should plan conservatively for Q3 and use the roadmap playbook we shared (link).
sam: will there be any changes to the IC -> TL promotion path during this window?
rachael: no changes to promotion criteria. we will delay formal interviews for cross-org promotion candidates if they conflict with transfer windows, but we won't block promotions. please coordinate with Lina if you've got candidates in the pipeline.
alex: @lina will you post the sign-off matrix + a short checklist for managers (handoff, on-call, customer comms, performance goals)?
lina: yes — checklist and template comms will be in the People Ops doc today. ping me if you need an exception.
dev-bot: deploy-note: "people-ops/transfer-policy.md" published to repo at 2456789120
sam: tiny ask — can we have a single Slack thread for all transfer exceptions? reduces noise.
rachael: agreed. use #people-ops-transfer-requests (I'll DM @lina to create it).
alex: appreciated. one last thing — who owns budget re-allocation when a headcount moves org? finance or hiring manager?
matt: finance sets the initial guidance; hiring manager must submit reallocation request. Finance + People Ops will fast-track priority approvals.
rachael: thanks all. I'll follow up with the slide updates and the doc links. :thumbsup:
__notes: Thread: All-hands follow-up Q&A on hiring, role transfers, sign-off, timelines, recruiter guidance, and operational continuity. Keep messages short and realistic for Slack.
